:::{#thm-matvec-columns}
#### A matrix-vector product combines the columns

If $\matr{A}$ is an $m \times n$ matrix
with columns $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n$
and $\vecf{x} \in \reals^n$, then

$$
\matr{A} \vecf{x} = x_1 \vecf{a}_1 + \cdots + x_n \vecf{a}_n.
$$

:::

::: proof

Compare entry $i$ of the two sides, for each $i = 1, \ldots, m$.
Entry $i$ of $\vecf{a}_j$ is $a_{ij}$, so

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} \vecf{x})_i
&= a_{i1} x_1 + \cdots + a_{in} x_n
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= x_1 a_{i1} + \cdots + x_n a_{in}
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)}
\\
&= (x_1 \vecf{a}_1 + \cdots + x_n \vecf{a}_n)_i
&& \text{(entry } i \text{ of each } x_j \vecf{a}_j \text{ is } x_j a_{ij} \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matvec-columns}
#### A product as a combination of columns

$$
\ba
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&= 1 \cd \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}
 + (-1) \cd \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-columns)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix},
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

the same answer as computing each entry as a row-times-vector dot product
(@rem-matvec-row-dot-products).

:::
